And I simply indicate that at this point to use the term my learned colleague used earlier of putting down a marker that we will be revisiting this issue in the near future with respect to reducing the scope of our exhibit list, but also perhaps suggesting alternative means by which evidence can be -- documentary evidence or other forms of tangible evidence can be put before the Trial Chamber other than through witnesses. Because to be quite frank and candid, Your Honours, at the rate we're going, the Prosecution will not get in all of the evidence by way of witness testimony that we envisioned. And again, this -- these are the types of issues that we're confronted with which lead us sometimes at the spur of the moment to make decisions on which issues to forego with a witness or which documents that were on the exhibit list listed for use with a witness to try to tender in through other witnesses simply because of the resource limitations -- time resource limitations that we operate under. And I offer this as an explanation for some of the decisions that were taken. Again, I categorically reject any suggestion that errors were made or mistakes were made. We are doing the absolute best that we can under the circumstances. I believe this trial has proceeded extremely smoothly, in terms of witness schedule and in terms of how the evidence has been put before Your Honours. I appreciate the collegial atmosphere that -- that this team enjoys with our colleagues across the courtroom. I would hope that that would continue. But I -- but I -- I feel duty-bound to -- to make the comments that I've made today in light of the comments made earlier by my -- by my friend Mr. Robson, and I don't believe there's anything further that I need to say on these issues. As I've indicated, we will continue doing what we can under the circumstances to put before Your Honours all the relevant evidence that we believe is important for the Trial Chamber to render the ultimate issue -- or to render the ultimate judgement that it is the Trial Chamber's duty to render. And I appreciate the opportunity to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'll just respond very briefly, Your Honour. First of all, the Defence, too, acknowledges that both parties are under restraints in this case. It applies to both the Defence as well as the Prosecution. But just turning to what prosecuting counsel just said, he objected to a submission that each and every witness will have evidence on the ultimate issue. The Defence don't seek to make that submission. In respect of the witness that the Trial Chamber heard yesterday and today, what we would submit is that Kadir Jusic was an important witness really in a key position, and he was someone who was able to speak as to matters that went to the heart of this case. I've heard what my learned friend says about each witness may come and tell one or two pieces of the puzzle, but in our submission, the one or two pieces of the puzzle that Mr. Jusic should have explained to the Court should have been done during his examination-in-chief and not during re-examination or even during questions following on from the Judges' questions. And in a nutshell, that was our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robson. I did ask in the beginning whether there was any relief sought by the Defence in making the submissions that they made. Mr. Robson indicated that they are -- all they are doing is to draw a mark. I guess I can close the discussion at that point. Thank you very much. Can you call the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as we indicated by way, I believe, of the Registry officer and the Trial Chamber's legal officer, the witness that was scheduled to testify yesterday and today has had to return to Bosnia and Herzegovina for personal reasons, and the witness who's scheduled to testify tomorrow is not yet ready to commence examination-in-chief, so we will reschedule the witness that was scheduled for yesterday and today and we will pick up with the schedule where it leaves off with the witness commencing tomorrow. And he will be -- his direct examination will be ready to start at 2.15 tomorrow. I expect to complete his examination-in-chief in less than the two hours indicated. Perhaps not significantly less, but I don't believe we'll be any longer than two hours, and I believe that should allow us to finish his testimony by Friday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. In -- in that event, then we're going to adjourn and reconvene tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in this courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
